skill.name: tmux
skill.description: Manage local tmux sessions for background tasks, interactive CLIs, and development services.
skill.summary: Control and monitor local tmux sessions from CLI, TUI, helper scripts, or TypeScript code.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: The core security risk is intentional local command execution through tmux, plus session input and pane-output capture. Most scanner findings are false positives from documentation paths, template strings, package integrity hashes, or bilingual Markdown. I also found unsafe shell-command rendering for unsanitized session IDs and temporary session metadata storage that should be hardened before broad publication.

remediation.issue: User-provided commands execute inside local tmux sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user intent before create runs a command, document the local execution boundary clearly, and avoid passing untrusted text into create.

remediation.issue: Generated attach and capture commands do not shell-quote session IDs.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict session names to a safe character set or shell-quote every generated command before printing or copying it.

remediation.issue: Session metadata is stored under the temporary directory by default.
remediation.suggestion: Create the socket directory and session store with owner-only permissions and consider placing metadata under a user-private state directory.

remediation.issue: Pane capture and timeout output can expose sensitive terminal text.
remediation.suggestion: Limit captured lines, avoid logging full captured output by default, and warn users before sharing terminal captures.

remediation.issue: The TUI uses a shell pipeline for clipboard copying.
remediation.suggestion: Use a direct clipboard API or a safely parameterized subprocess call, and quote command text before copying.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Command Rendering for Session IDs
semantic_findings.description: Session IDs include the caller-supplied session name and are later rendered into attach or capture shell commands without shell quoting. A crafted session name could create dangerous copy-paste commands in CLI or TUI output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The session ID is built directly from name and category, then printed or copied as a shell command. Exploitation requires a crafted session name or tampered session metadata, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Session Metadata Stored in Shared Temporary Directory
semantic_findings.description: The default socket directory and session store are under /tmp, and the session JSON includes command strings and tmux targets. On shared systems, permissive file modes or tampering could expose commands or influence cleanup and attach behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default configuration stores state under TMPDIR or /tmp and saveSessions writes JSON without an explicit file mode. The impact depends on host umask and filesystem isolation.

content.user_title: Manage tmux Sessions for Agent Workflows
content.value_statement: Long-running terminal tasks are hard to start, monitor, and clean up across agent sessions. This skill provides CLI, TUI, script, and TypeScript helpers for controlled local tmux session management.
actual_capabilities: Create named tmux sessions on a private socket and track session metadata.
List, inspect, synchronize, and clean up task, service, and agent sessions.
Send literal input to an existing tmux pane and capture recent pane output.
Use the workflow through a CLI, an Ink-based TUI, helper shell scripts, or a TypeScript API.
Wait for expected text in tmux output when automating long-running terminal tasks.
limitations: Requires tmux, Bun, and Bash on the local machine.
Runs user-provided shell commands inside local tmux sessions.
Stores session state in temporary local files and TUI preferences in a home-directory config file.
Does not manage remote hosts, cloud terminals, or network orchestration.

use_cases.title: Run Background Development Tasks
use_cases.description: Start build watchers, test runners, and local services, then inspect output without blocking the main agent session.

use_cases.title: Operate Interactive CLIs
use_cases.description: Create a persistent terminal session for REPLs, debuggers, and database shells, then send literal input when needed.

use_cases.title: Monitor Agent Workloads
use_cases.description: Track long-running jobs by category, capture recent output, and clean up stale sessions after inactivity.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one background command.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tmux task session named build-check that runs my project build. Show me the session ID and how to monitor it.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Running Sessions
prompt_templates.scenario: Check current work without attaching to every pane.
prompt_templates.prompt: List my tmux sessions, sync their status, and capture the latest output from any running service sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Drive an Interactive Tool
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a REPL or debugger that needs follow-up input.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Python REPL session, send a simple expression, capture the output, and keep the session available.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Multi-Service Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced local development workflow with cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start separate tmux sessions for the app server, test watcher, and build watcher. Wait for ready text where possible, then summarize status and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Create a task session for a long build and tell me how to follow it.
output: A new task session is created with a unique session ID.
The response includes an attach instruction and a capture instruction.
The session remains available for later status checks or cleanup.

output_examples.input: Show me what my running service session is doing.
output: The skill syncs stored session state with tmux.
It reports the selected session status and recent pane output.
It does not attach interactively unless requested.

output_examples.input: Clean up stale tmux sessions older than one day.
output: Old inactive sessions are terminated through tmux.
The local session metadata file is updated.
The result states how many sessions were cleaned.

best_practices: Use short session names with letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores.
Run only commands you trust because create starts a real local shell command.
Review captured pane output before sharing it because terminal output can contain secrets.
anti_patterns: Do not run untrusted shell commands through create.
Do not use untrusted session names in generated attach commands.
Do not rely on temporary session files as an access-control boundary.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands on my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. The create command starts user-provided commands inside local tmux sessions.

faq.question: Can it work without tmux?
faq.answer: No. tmux is required because the skill manages tmux sessions and panes.

faq.question: Can I use a visual interface?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes an Ink-based terminal UI for listing, capturing, attaching, and killing sessions.

faq.question: Where does it store state?
faq.answer: It stores session metadata in a temporary local JSON file and TUI preferences in a home-directory config file.

faq.question: Does it send data to the network?
faq.answer: No evidence found of network requests. A localhost URL appears only inside a demo command string.

faq.question: Is captured output always safe to share?
faq.answer: No. Captured terminal output may include tokens, logs, paths, or other sensitive local data.
